newsitem.title: USA: Excite CEO sees breakeven in H1 1998.
newsitem.headline: Excite CEO sees breakeven in H1 1998.

text.p: Excite Inc Chief Executive Officer George Bell said the company is comfortable with Wall Street consensus estimates for Excite to reach break-even in first half 1998.

Bell said a blending of consensus estimates -- with some analysts predicting first quarter break-even and others projecting the Internet search and navigation company won't hit break even until the second quarter next year -- was for it to cross breakeven sometime in April.

Bell also said Excite, which is developing into a media company on the Internet, expects the overall market for advertising on the Internet this year to be around $600 million -- more than double 1996 levels, but only slightly more than half one estimate of $1.1 billion.

Bell told reporters after a presentation to a Robertson Stephens investment conference here that he expects two distinct advertising trends to continue: downward pressure on bulk banner advertising for general rotation and growth of higher-rate differentiated space.

Noting that Excite's average cost per thousand (CPM) was hovering just under $20 in the second quarter, roughly typical for the leading search engines, he said there was "a lot of pressure on tonnage" general rotation space.
Internet media companies sell advertising by posting banners on which visitors may click to be transferred to an advertiser-designated Web page.

In addition to general rotation, for which there is a lot of excess capacity, most companies like Excite now also offer the capability to sell advertisements linked to certain keywords typed in by customers, or by subjects.

Bell said that, while he had heard of deals being struck at $3 to $4 per CPM for general rotation ads, Excite has been able to develop a $35 to $38 price point for its newly created "channels", which offer information by subject.

Such channels accounted for nearly half of Excite's capacity in the second quarter, he said. Excite has recently been averaging around 16 million page views a day, up from around 15 million in the first quarter.
"Most of us (the search engine companies) were sold out on the important key words," he said, referring to the first quarter's results.
The traffic rates exclude the Netfinder search capability that Excite provides America Online Inc, which would have brought the average to 21-22 million page views a day.

Bell noted that Excite has used acquisitions and investments to climb to the number two Internet search and navigation company, behind Yahoo! Inc., from the seventh-ranked position 16 months ago. Yahoo! reported that its number of page views per day averaged 38 million in June, up by around eight million from the month of March.
